label: digit 0 read during the original (input) phase
explanation: Fires on every step where the input token is the digit 0 while the original sequence is being read (t < L), at any position and for any L; precision 1.0 on dev. Magnitude is fairly uniform (about 0.7-1.0 of max). It is highest when the 0 comes late in the sequence just before <DEL> (top examples are a 0 at the last original position), and weaker for early 0s (about 0.7). It does not fire on the 0 when it is fed back during the copy phase, at the delimiter, or on other digits and letters. The only stray activations are tiny (about 0.15 of max) on an e right after a 0 at t=1, and on the copy-phase step after an echoed leading 0.

issues: The magnitude description is slightly off. A 0 at t=0 fires at about 0.92 of max (the misses output shows *[0:0.92]* at step 0 every time), so it is not 'weak early'. The profile is U-shaped: about 1.0 for a 0 in the last original position, about 0.92 at t=0, and lowest (about 0.64-0.8) for 0s in the middle positions.

The stray activations match the explanation and are small. On the test split there are 1452 missed steps holding 0.2% of activation mass. They are an e at t=1 right after a leading 0 (about 0.15 of max), and the copy step with recall_idx=1 after an echoed leading 0 (about 0.15 of max). Precision on test is 1.0 with 0 false positives.

The other claims check out on test: precision 1.0, recall 0.987, F1 0.993, mass recall 0.998. It never fires on the delimiter (0 active steps), copy-phase mass is 0.001, and the firing rate is the same at every L and orig_idx (about 0.033-0.035).
